[0] Apple most likely as early as next week to showcase their newly co-developed smart home accessories. Before the exhibition begins, a leaker today has leaked a new HomeKit feature exclusive to these "second-party" accessories.

[1] 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Sony's range of BRAVIA TVs are currently having a massive sale, covering everything from entry-level models to flagship units, with some models supporting AirPlay 2 — buy now and enjoy the discount!

[2] HomeKit Exclusive New Feature

[3] Earlier this week, Aaron Perris spotted clues in the code about a new feature that "nearby smart home accessories can display controls in the Dynamic Island." Now, @itspdfu has found more details on how this feature works.

[4] In a social media post today, pdfu said that Apple and LG's co-developed "second-party" home accessories will support a brand new "Proximity Control" feature.

[5] When you tap or bring your iPhone close to an LG accessory, the Dynamic Island will pop up a notification. The notification will display an "Open Controls" button for controlling accessories like thermostats; for cameras and doorbells, it will show "Camera View."

[6] The account explained:

[7] When you first tap the accessory to pair it, during the setup process initiated by the iPhone, the Dynamic Island will also show related feedback. The principle behind it is that the accessory writes an "apple-deviceid" into the Matter data content stored on its NFC tag, helping iOS identify the device when tapped. It will also broadcast a Bluetooth Low Energy signal used for Apple Proximity Control.

[8] It seems users can choose to turn off this feature in the Home app. However, note that features appearing in Apple's code may not necessarily launch, and even if they do, the actual operation may differ significantly from what's currently seen.

[9] Even so, this is clearly an example of a feature exclusive to "second-party" accessories. Bloomberg first reported this week on the collaboration between Apple and LG, detailing the smart home products the two companies are developing together, including thermostats, deadbolt locks, indoor security cameras, outdoor security cameras, and floodlight cameras.

[10] In the following days, we have seen many other leaks about this plan:

  • [11] Apple's new Home "second-party" accessories are larger in scale than expected, revealed by leaks
  • [12] Leaked images reveal new smart door locks, thermostats and other products developed by Apple for LG
  • [13] Leaked images reveal new Home cameras and doorbells from the Apple-LG collaboration

[14] According to Bloomberg, these accessories "will be at least a few more months" before being officially launched by Apple. They may still appear at next week's Apple "Welcome home" event.
